title: The smooth affine scheme of isomorphisms of two group scheme torsors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H$ a group object in schemes over $S$: an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity and inversion satisfying the group diagrams. Assume $H\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $Y$ be an $S$-scheme and $P\to Y$, $Q\to Y$ be represented right $H$-torsors [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. For every $Y$-scheme $T$ put $P_T=P\times_YT$, $Q_T=Q\times_YT$ and $H_T=H\times_ST$. The functor sending $T$ to the set of $T$-isomorphisms $P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_T$ commuting with the right $H_T$-actions is represented by a $Y$-scheme $I=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}_H(P,Q)$, and $I\to Y$ is affine and smooth; if $Y$ is affine, $I$ is an affine scheme. For every morphism $Y'\to Y$, the canonical morphism $I\times_YY'\to\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}_{H_{Y'}}(P_{Y'},Q_{Y'})$ is an isomorphism. In particular a section of $I\to Y$ is exactly a right $H$-torsor isomorphism $P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$.

source.place: Tag 04AG (section-not-algebraic-stack), paragraph identifying the affine diagonal with the scheme Isom(P_1,P_2); the same fpqc descent argument applies over any base scheme. Smoothness is the torsor-local smoothness assertion used in Alper--Halpern-Leistner--Heinloth, Cartan--Iwahori--Matsumoto decompositions, Section 2, Claim 3, printed p.3; author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf, WANTED locally.

proof.text: The torsor definition makes $P\to Y$ and $Q\to Y$ flat, surjective and quasi-compact. Each is an fpqc singleton cover: above an affine open $W\subset Y$, its inverse image is quasi-compact and has a finite affine open cover; surjectivity says the images of those opens cover $W$, exactly the fpqc definition. Put $U=P\times_YQ$. Base change of the cover $Q\to Y$ to $P$, followed by composition with the cover $P\to Y$, shows that $u:U\to Y$ is an fpqc singleton cover. It is also quasi-compact: above each affine $W\subset Y$, $P_W$ is quasi-compact, the map $U_W\to P_W$ is quasi-compact by base change of $Q\to Y$, and the quasi-compact-source conclusion of the permanence lemma makes $U_W$ quasi-compact. Thus $u$ is flat, quasi-compact and surjective. The projections $U\to P,Q$ give sections $p\in P_U(U)$ and $q\in Q_U(U)$.

source.place: Tags 022B (definition-fpqc-covering), 022D (lemma-fpqc), parts (2),(3); singleton covers supplied by the represented torsor hypothesis.

proof.text: The torsor isomorphism $(x,h)\mapsto(x,xh)$, pulled back along $p$, gives an equivariant isomorphism $H_U\xrightarrow{\sim}P_U$, $h\mapsto ph$; its inverse sends $x$ to the unique $h$ with $x=ph$. The section $q$ gives $H_U\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_U$ in the same way. For any $U$-scheme $T$, an equivariant isomorphism is uniquely $f_c(ph)=qch$ for a morphism $c:T\to H_U$ over $U$: evaluate it at $p$ to obtain $c$, and use equivariance. Conversely this formula is an isomorphism, with inverse $qk\mapsto p c^{-1}k$. These are scheme morphisms, being composites of the torsor trivializations, multiplication and inversion, and they commute with every change of $T$. Consequently $V=H\times_SU$ represents the isomorphism functor after restriction to $U$.

source.place: Tag 04AG (section-not-algebraic-stack), paragraph on Isom(P_1,P_2): explicit trivial-torsor calculation, valid over any base.

proof.text: On $U_2=U\times_YU$ write $p_0,p_1$ and $q_0,q_1$ for the two pairs of sections. The inverse of the torsor isomorphism produces morphisms $a_{01},b_{01}:U_2\to H$ over $S$ characterized by $p_1=p_0a_{01}$ and $q_1=q_0b_{01}$. The same map $f$ has parameters $c_0,c_1$ satisfying $q_0c_0a_{01}=f(p_1)=q_1c_1$, hence $c_1=b_{01}^{-1}c_0a_{01}$. Define $\theta_{01}:\mathrm{pr}_0^*V\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ by this formula; its inverse is $c_1\mapsto b_{01}c_1a_{01}^{-1}$. On $U_3=U\times_YU\times_YU$, uniqueness of division in each torsor gives $a_{02}=a_{01}a_{12}$ and $b_{02}=b_{01}b_{12}$. Therefore $\theta_{12}(\theta_{01}(c))=b_{12}^{-1}b_{01}^{-1}c a_{01}a_{12}=b_{02}^{-1}c a_{02}=\theta_{02}(c)$. This is the required descent cocycle. No commutativity of $H$ is used.

source.place: Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum), cocycle condition; transition calculation for the Isom scheme of Tag 04AG.

proof.text: The morphism $V=H\times_SU\to U$ is affine by affine-morphism base change. Apply effective descent for affine morphisms to this $V$, its cocycle $\theta$, and the singleton fpqc cover $u$. It supplies a scheme $I\to Y$ and an isomorphism $I\times_YU\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ identifying its canonical descent datum with $\theta$. Thus it supplies the precise overlap compatibility calculated in the preceding step, rather than just an abstract local isomorphism.

The projection $I\times_YU\to U$ is identified with $H\times_SU\to U$. It is affine by base change and smooth by the smooth-base-change clause of the proper-and-smooth permanence node, applied to $H\to S$ and $U\to S$; that clause assumes smoothness alone, not properness. Affineness descends along the fpqc singleton cover $U\to Y$. Smoothness descends along the same map, whose flatness, quasi-compactness and surjectivity were verified in step 1. Hence $I\to Y$ is affine and smooth. If $Y$ is affine, the affine-source clause of affine-morphism permanence gives that $I$ is affine.

For any $T\to Y$, the base-changed singleton $U_T=T\times_YU\to T$ is fpqc. Morphisms $T\to I$ over $Y$ are the compatible maps $U_T\to I$ over $Y$, by representable fpqc descent; being over $Y$ is checked after the cover by uniqueness. Using $I_U\simeq V$, these are exactly parameters $c:U_T\to H$ over $S$ with $c_1=b_{01}^{-1}c_0a_{01}$. By steps 2 and 3 those parameters give isomorphisms $(P_T)_{U_T}\to(Q_T)_{U_T}$ agreeing on overlaps. Apply representable fpqc descent to the base-changed cover of $P_T$ to descend these morphisms into $Q_T$, and to the cover of $Q_T$ to descend their inverses. Their composites are identities, and their structure maps agree with those of $P_T,Q_T$, since each equality holds after the corresponding fpqc cover and descent gives uniqueness. Equivariance is the equality of two maps $P_T\times_T H_T\to Q_T$; these too agree after the base-changed fpqc cover, hence agree globally. Conversely any equivariant torsor isomorphism restricts to the unique parameters of step 2, satisfying exactly the displayed transition relation. The two constructions are inverse. All restrictions, formulas and descended morphisms commute with a map $T'\to T$, by the same uniqueness. This proves the natural representing bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(T,I)\cong\operatorname{Isom}_{H_T}(P_T,Q_T)$.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), applied to T, P_T, Q_T and P_T times_T H_T; topologies.tex Tag 022D(3).

proof.text: Let $Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. For a $Y'$-scheme $T$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(T,I\times_YY')$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(T,I)$. It also identifies $(P_{Y'})_T=P_T$, $(Q_{Y'})_T=Q_T$, and $(H_{Y'})_T=H_T$, including their actions. The representing bijection of step 6 therefore shows that $I\times_YY'$ represents precisely the isomorphism functor for the two pulled-back torsors. These remain torsors: their singleton cover is flat, surjective and finitely presented by fpqc base change and finite-presentation permanence, and their action and torsor isomorphism pull back. Applying the construction to them gives its second representing scheme. The resulting natural isomorphism between the two representable functors, and its inverse, are represented by mutually inverse morphisms by Yoneda full faithfulness; this is the asserted canonical base-change isomorphism. Finally evaluating the bijection of step 6 at $T=Y$ identifies sections of $I\to Y$ with the required torsor isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda), full faithfulness, after the fibre-product universal property; base change of the torsor hypotheses via topologies.tex Tag 022D and morphisms.tex Tag 01TS.
